summary: SF_ARCH_ELEMENT_NC_v1 passes QA with 5 minor warnings and 0 blockers. All 5 pipeline files reviewed (spec.json pending assembly). Cross-file threading validated: 39 TSK_ARCH_* IDs in sop_modules match 39 rates in production. Three paintable items with distinct UOMs: ITM_ARCH_BEAM (LF), ITM_ARCH_COLUMN (EA), ITM_ARCH_MANTEL (EA). Combined prime+paint with primer conditional on substrate_state. 5 substrate-driven primer systems + 3 QT-driven finish systems, all reusing existing SYS_ IDs. Three element-specific complexity modifiers: beam_profile (1.0-1.40x), column_type (1.0-1.30x), mantel_type (1.0-1.50x) — each correctly scoped to its own item only. 4 protection zones all properly paired setup/teardown. Localized floor protection (floor_workzone, not floor_full) correctly chosen for discrete elements. Height modifier via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND applies to beam and column tasks. Sheen/QT gate compatible (QT3+satin default). Human Feedback Gate has NOT occurred — expected for v0.1.0 draft.

issues.description: Beam, column, and mantel production rates are research estimates with no canonical doctrine values. Beam spray 150 LF/hr, brush 60 LF/hr (from research guidance 130-170 and 50-70 midpoints). Column spray 5 EA/hr, brush 2.5 EA/hr (research 4-6 and 2-3). Mantel spray 2.5 EA/hr, brush 1.5 EA/hr (research 2-3 and 1-2). Beam overhead factor ~0.85x of equivalent trim rates. All flagged as assumptions (A-001 through A-007).

key_characteristics: First spec with 3 paintable items having 3 DIFFERENT UOMs: beam (LF), column (EA), mantel (EA). Most complex multi-item architecture in the system.

Per-element tasks where UOM differs: sand, fill, caulk, prime, spray/brush finish, interstage sand — each has separate beam/column/mantel tasks. 27 per-element tasks + 12 shared FIXED/room-level tasks = 39 total.
Three element-specific complexity modifiers, each scoped exclusively: beam_profile (1.0-1.40x), column_type (1.0-1.30x), mantel_type (1.0-1.50x).

Mixed working heights within a single spec: beams are overhead (ceiling-mounted), columns are full-height (floor-to-ceiling), mantels are wall-height (H1 typical). Height modifier via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND applies to beams and columns.
Beam overhead factor ~0.85x baked into base rates — less severe than full ceiling (0.70-0.80x) because beams are discrete elements, not continuous overhead surfaces.
Localized protection (floor_workzone, not floor_full) — correct for discrete elements that are not room-spanning.
39 tasks total (24 binary, 15 qt_scaled) — comparable to SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC (43 tasks, 4 items).
3 proposed PaintScope keys — one per paintable item. All 7 existing PaintScope keys reused.
All 8 material system IDs reuse existing entries — 5 primer SYS_ + 3 finish SYS_ — REUSE OVER CREATION.
QT2 prohibited (prominent millwork). QT3+satin default has no sheen/QT gate tension.
COMP_FIREPLACE cross-spec note: mantels are the SOURCE of COMP_FIREPLACE complexity for adjacent wall/ceiling specs — this spec is not affected by it.
review_notes: Architectural element spec is the most complex multi-item spec in the system with 3 paintable items across 3 different UOMs (LF, EA, EA). The per-element task architecture is well-designed — separate tasks where UOM/geometry differs, shared FIXED tasks for room-level work. Protection zones are appropriately localized (floor_workzone, not floor_full) reflecting that these are discrete elements, not room-spanning surfaces. The three complexity modifier sets are each correctly scoped to their respective element type with no cross-application. Research-based production rates are reasonable midpoints with documented range bounds and assumptions. No critical or major issues found. 5 minor warnings are all documentation/naming/field-validation items, not structural problems.
